subject: ela
title: Sound-Spelling and Word Reading
summary: A five-day, adult-supported bridge from phoneme work and short-vowel words into digraphs, long-vowel patterns, two-syllable words, endings, and irregular words.

materials.name: Letter cards including common digraphs
alternatives: letters and digraphs written on paper squares

materials.name: Three to six small sound counters
Word cards for the patterns being taught
alternatives: words written in large print on paper strips

materials.name: A short controlled text limited to taught patterns
alternatives: adult-written controlled sentences checked word by word

days.title: Hear, Blend, and Segment Every Sound
days.objective: I can blend a spoken word and separate it into phonemes in order.
adultSetup: Choose five familiar one-syllable words with three or four phonemes.
Use a natural adult voice for isolated phonemes and avoid adding an extra vowel to consonant sounds.
days.textRecommendation: Use a playful rhyme or poem as an oral-language warm-up, then select only familiar words for explicit sound work.

directions: Say two rhyming words and notice the shared ending.
Stretch one continuous sound and contrast it with one quick stop sound.
Push one counter for each sound in a word without showing letters first.
Sweep beneath the counters while blending the sounds back into the word.
Identify the first, last, and vowel sound after the whole word is known.
Blend two adult-segmented words.
Segment two words with counters and check by blending them again.
Correct order errors by returning to the spoken word rather than spelling from memory.
Complete five reviewed phoneme and vowel-sound items with spoken adult support for isolated sounds.
Do not let text-to-speech pronunciation of slash notation replace the adult sound model.
Change one sound in a practiced word and blend the new word.
Use two- or three-phoneme words and one counter per sound.
Model and copy one word before asking for an independent response.
Avoid printed letters until the oral sequence is stable.

masteryEvidence: Blends and segments at least three familiar one-syllable words in order.
Identifies a requested beginning, ending, or vowel sound without relying on printed choices alone.

days.title: Read Digraphs and Consonant Clusters
days.objective: I can recognize common digraphs and blend them in one-syllable words.
adultSetup: Prepare cards for sh, ch, th, wh, ng, and ck plus known single letters.
Choose controlled words that use known short vowels and only one new consonant pattern at a time.
days.textRecommendation: Choose a decodable passage or adult-written sentences limited to known short vowels and the digraphs explicitly taught that day.

directions: Review two known CVC words.
Place s and h together and explain that the pair represents one sound in the target words.
Build a word such as ship and mark sh as one sound-spelling unit.
Blend from left to right without separating the digraph.
Contrast a word with a digraph and a word with two separately pronounced consonants.
Sort words by their beginning or ending digraph.
Build and blend several controlled words with letter cards.
Read one controlled sentence and point to the taught pattern.
Complete five reviewed blending, phoneme, digraph, and one-syllable word items.
Read each target word before using a picture or meaning check.
Find taught digraphs in a familiar book without requiring every surrounding word to be read.
Teach one digraph with two contrasting word choices.
Underline or connect the two letters so they move as one unit.
Return to oral blending before asking for sentence reading.

masteryEvidence: Reads controlled one-syllable words containing at least two taught digraphs.
Keeps the digraph together as one sound-spelling unit while blending.

days.title: Compare Short and Long Vowel Patterns
days.objective: I can compare short- and long-vowel words and use a taught pattern to read them.
adultSetup: Prepare a small set of reviewed final-e word pairs such as cap and cape or kit and kite.
Prepare cards for the common vowel teams oa and ee, and keep the controlled text limited to the final-e and vowel-team patterns explicitly taught.
days.textRecommendation: Use a short controlled text that contrasts reviewed short-vowel words with explicitly taught final-e, oa, and ee words; preteach any essential irregular word.

directions: Read two known short-vowel words.
Listen to one short and one long vowel sound in familiar words and name what changes.
Build a short-vowel word, read it, then add final e and reread.
Model oa in boat and ee in seed as two-letter teams that represent a long vowel sound.
Check each pronunciation by matching the letters to the taught pattern and asking whether it makes a recognizable word.
Transform reviewed final-e word pairs with letter cards.
Sort a small set into short-vowel, final-e, oa, and ee patterns.
Read controlled phrases and explain which spelling pattern helped.
Complete five reviewed vowel-sound, one-syllable decoding, and long-vowel items.
Read the whole target before selecting an answer and avoid untaught vowel teams in adult-created examples.
Make and illustrate two related short/long word pairs from reviewed patterns.
Use one word pair and color-independent marks under the vowel positions.
Read each word after every card change.
Do not introduce a second long-vowel spelling until the first contrast is reliable.

masteryEvidence: Reads several reviewed short/long contrast words using their spelling patterns.
Explains the relevant difference without overgeneralizing the pattern to every word.

days.title: Use Syllables and Endings
days.objective: I can break a word into syllables and use a familiar ending to help read it.
adultSetup: Prepare familiar compound and two-syllable word cards.
Prepare base-word cards with reviewed endings such as s, ed, and ing.
days.textRecommendation: Choose several controlled sentences containing only reviewed two-syllable words and endings; avoid presenting syllable labels as a substitute for decoding.

directions: Clap the syllables in several familiar names and objects.
Read a known base word and then the same word with s or ing.
Mark the spoken syllables in a familiar two-syllable word and connect them to printed parts.
Read a base word first, then attach and read its ending.
Explain how an ending can change meaning or time while the base remains recognizable.
Divide and blend several familiar two-syllable words.
Build base-word and ending combinations, reading each complete word.
Use the resulting words in short oral or printed sentences.
Complete five reviewed syllable, two-syllable decoding, and ending items.
For one word, cover the ending, read the base, uncover the ending, and reread.
Make a small word family chart from one base word and several reviewed endings.
Use a familiar compound whose two parts are independently readable.
Say, mark, and read each part before blending the whole.
Teach one ending at a time and compare it with the unchanged base.

masteryEvidence: Uses a meaningful division to read familiar two-syllable words.
Reads a known base word with at least two reviewed endings and explains one meaning change.

days.title: Read Regular and Irregular Words in Text
days.objective: I can use sound-spelling patterns and remembered irregular parts to read a controlled text.
adultSetup: Prepare a short controlled text using patterns taught during the week.
Choose no more than two essential irregular words and mark their regular and unexpected parts.
days.textRecommendation: Use four to eight connected sentences whose sound-spelling demands have been checked against the learner's taught scope; reread the same text for accuracy before fluency.

directions: Review one word from each taught pattern.
Analyze one irregular word by identifying the parts that work as expected and the part to remember.
Read the first controlled sentence from left to right and model solving one unfamiliar regular word.
Model recognizing an explicitly taught irregular word without pretending every part is decodable.
Reread the sentence smoothly only after it is accurate.
Alternate sentences with the learner and discuss one decoding choice per sentence.
Prompt self-correction when a pronunciation does not fit the letters or sentence meaning.
Reread a short section with less adult support.
Complete six cumulative reviewed phonics and word-recognition items.
Then read the controlled text independently while the adult records patterns used, self-corrections, and any supplied words.
Illustrate the controlled text and write or dictate one additional sentence using reviewed patterns.
Return to one error pattern and a word-card model.
Practice two parallel words, then reread only the sentence containing that pattern.
Supply untaught words directly rather than turning them into an unplanned decoding test.

masteryEvidence: Reads a short controlled text with accurate use of taught patterns and recorded support level.
Distinguishes pattern-based decoding from the explicitly remembered part of an irregular word.
Self-corrects at least one mismatch when appropriate; speed is not used as the sole mastery criterion.

accommodationNotes: Read directions aloud and provide replay without penalty, but do not use ordinary TTS as an isolated-phoneme model.
Use large high-contrast print, tactile letters, and sound counters when helpful.
Accept pointing, moving cards, eye gaze, signing, or speech when handwriting is not being assessed.
Teach fewer patterns at once and provide additional accurate rereading without treating the accommodation as failed mastery.

review.notes: Machine-validated instructional draft. It requires named human curriculum review and controlled-text inspection before production use.
